extracted.intended_audience: photographers, photo editors, and media organizations submitting work to the 82nd Pictures of the Year competition
extracted.subtask_description: Category definitions and submission/eligibility rules for the 82nd Annual Pictures of the Year competition, describing what kinds of single images, series, portfolios, or multimedia entries belong in each category and specific format/publication/date requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: 1 - Science & Natural History
rubrics_metrics.description: A single photograph that increases the understanding and appreciation of science or the natural world.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Studio scenes that are arranged by the photographer are not eligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: 2 - Science & Natural History Picture Story
rubrics_metrics.description: A narrative picture story, essay, sequence, or series that increases the understanding and appreciation for science or the natural world.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Studio scenes that are arranged by the photographer are not eligible. 10 photographs maximum per entry.

rubrics_metrics.name: 3 - General News
rubrics_metrics.description: A single photograph of a news event or social issue for which planning was possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: 4 - Impact 2024: U.S. Presidential 2024
rubrics_metrics.description: A single photograph that captures the mood, emotion, character, interaction, or campaign environment of the U.S. presidential election.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Photograph must be taken during 2024.

rubrics_metrics.name: 5 - Impact 2024: Campaign 2024
rubrics_metrics.description: A single photograph that captures the mood, emotion, character, interaction, or campaign environment during a race for local or state elections (non-presidential).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Photograph must be taken during 2024.

rubrics_metrics.name: 6 - Spot News
rubrics_metrics.description: A single photograph of a breaking news event for which no planning was possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: 7 - Daily Life
rubrics_metrics.description: A single, unposed photograph that reflects the human experience, celebrates life, or chronicles a cultural trend.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respect for the dignity of the person is important.

rubrics_metrics.name: 8 - Portrait
rubrics_metrics.description: A single photograph that reflects a strong sense of a person’s identity or narrative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respect for the dignity of the person is important.

rubrics_metrics.name: 9 - Portrait Series
rubrics_metrics.description: A series of photographs that reflects a strong sense of identity or narrative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respect for the dignity of the person is important. 10 photographs maximum per entry.

rubrics_metrics.name: 10 - National/International News Picture Story
rubrics_metrics.description: A narrative picture story based on daily coverage of a general or breaking news event that is of primary interest to an entire nation or the world.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is usually created with the intent to share nationally or internationally. 10 photographs maximum per story.

rubrics_metrics.name: 11 - Issue Reporting Picture Story
rubrics_metrics.description: A narrative picture story that explores an important social, economic, or political issue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 10 photographs maximum per story.

rubrics_metrics.name: 12 - Daily Life Picture Story
rubrics_metrics.description: A narrative picture story that reflects the everyday human experience, celebrates life, or chronicles a cultural trend.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respect for the dignity of the person is important. 10 photographs maximum per story.

rubrics_metrics.name: 13 - Local News Picture Story
rubrics_metrics.description: A narrative picture story based on daily coverage of a general or breaking news event that is of primary interest to the local audience in a media organization or the photographer’s primary geographic market (a hometown story).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 10 photographs maximum per story.

rubrics_metrics.name: 14 - Impact 2024: On the Campaign Trail
rubrics_metrics.description: A narrative picture story based on coverage of campaigns, rallies or protests related to local and national elections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 10 photographs maximum per story.

rubrics_metrics.name: 16 - Sports Action
rubrics_metrics.description: A single photograph that captures peak action of an individual or team sport.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Jubilation, dejection, or reaction images should be entered in the Sports Life and Recreational category. Photographs must be taken during 2024.

rubrics_metrics.name: 17 - Sports Life and Recreational Sports
rubrics_metrics.description: A single photograph that celebrates the role that professional or amateur sports play in a community; may show emotional highlights of players or fans’ reactions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Photographs must be taken during 2024.

rubrics_metrics.name: 18 - Sports Picture Story
rubrics_metrics.description: A narrative picture story or series of images that increases the understanding of the role that professional or amateur athletics play in the lives of athletes and their community.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Story may focus on sports as a catalyst of change in gender, race, political, and cultural issues. 10 photographs maximum per story.

rubrics_metrics.name: 19 – Olympics Sports Action
rubrics_metrics.description: Single photographs that capture the peak action of individual or team competition in the 2024 Summer Olympics in Paris.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Jubilation, dejection, and reaction photographs should be entered in the Olympics Sports Life category.

rubrics_metrics.name: 20 – Olympics Sports Life
rubrics_metrics.description: A single photograph that increases the understanding and appreciation for sports or celebrates the role that athletics play in the lives of athletes and fans at the 2024 Summer Olympics in Paris.

rubrics_metrics.name: 21 - Documentary News Reporting (video)
rubrics_metrics.description: A single video covering general or breaking news; may explore a social, economic or political issue (flexible length – up to about 15 minutes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enter longer stories in “Documentary of the Year.” Open to teams or individuals; list all contributors in the credit field. Include a .jpg thumbnail, a URL link and required username and password.

rubrics_metrics.name: 22 - Documentary Daily Life (video)
rubrics_metrics.description: A single video that reflects the human experience, celebrates life, or chronicles a cultural trend (flexible length – up to about 15 minutes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enter longer stories in “Documentary of the Year.” Open to teams or individuals; list all contributors in the credit field. Include a .jpg thumbnail, a URL link and required username and password.

rubrics_metrics.name: 23 - Documentary of the Year (video)
rubrics_metrics.description: Premiere category recognizing excellence in longform video reporting that focuses on news, a social issue or cultural trend (about 15-45 minutes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not enter shorter versions in other categories. Open to teams or individuals; list all contributors in the credit field. Include a .jpg thumbnail, a URL link and required username and password.

rubrics_metrics.name: 24 - Online Storytelling: Daily Life
rubrics_metrics.description: A single daily life story presented on an online platform such as a website or social media; may be coverage of an issue, everyday human experience, or a cultural trend.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Story must have been shot, produced, or published for the first time in 2024. If published across multiple platforms, choose the single platform that best represents the story. Updated versions of the originally posted story are acceptable. Web pages that present only a single video should be submitted in the documentary categories. Multi-chapter/page stories should be entered in Online Storytelling Project of the Year; if entering a single story from a series, clearly indicate which single story will be reviewed. Include a .jpg thumbnail and an active URL link for each story. Include required username and password.

rubrics_metrics.name: 25 - Online Storytelling: News Reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: A single news story presented on an online platform; may be coverage of an issue or daily news.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Story must have been shot, produced, or published for the first time in 2024. If published across multiple platforms, choose the one platform that best represents that specific story. Updated versions are acceptable. Web pages that present a single video should be entered in the documentary categories. Multi-chapter/page stories go in Online Storytelling Project of the Year; if entering a single story from a series, clearly indicate which single story should be reviewed. Submit a .jpg thumbnail and an active URL link for each story. Include required username and password.

rubrics_metrics.name: 26 - Online Storytelling Project of the Year
rubrics_metrics.description: Premiere category appraising in-depth visual online journalism that explores a social, economic, or political issue through a special report, series, or multiple chapters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Open to teams or individuals. Submit a .jpg thumbnail and an active URL link for each story. Include required usernames and passwords.

rubrics_metrics.name: 27 - Newspaper Picture Editing
rubrics_metrics.description: A single published story from the coverage of an issue, daily life, or news in a general circulation newspaper; may include one or more pages from up to 5 issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All stories must be published in 2024. Include a story summary in the description field. We cannot accept .pdf files—convert all .pdf files to .jpg files. Submit each page as a separate .jpg file. A double truck (two facing pages) should be submitted as a single .jpg file.

rubrics_metrics.name: 28 - Magazine Picture Editing
rubrics_metrics.description: A single published story from the coverage of daily life, news or a social issue in a magazine or specialty publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All stories must be published in 2024. We cannot accept .pdf files—convert all .pdf files to .jpg files. Stories may be entered only once and attributed to a single editor; the same story cannot be entered by two people. Submit each page as a separate .jpg file. A double truck (two facing pages) should be submitted as a single .jpg file.

rubrics_metrics.name: 29 - Visual Editor of the Year
rubrics_metrics.description: Premiere category awarding editing excellence to one person; newspaper, magazine, and online visual editors may enter with a portfolio representing work where they served as lead editor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All stories must be published in 2024. Editors are encouraged to use the description field to describe their role in reporting and presentation. Portfolio may include content published online and in print and may present up to 10 stories, either in print or online. A converged print-and-online version of a specific story counts as one story. If needed, include an active URL link and required usernames and passwords. Stories may be entered only once and attributed to a single editor; the same story cannot be included in multiple entries. We cannot accept .pdf files—convert all .pdf files to .jpg files. Submit each page as a separate .jpg file. A double truck should be submitted as a single .jpg file. Team entries should be entered in the 'Angus McDougall Excellence in Editing Award.'

rubrics_metrics.name: 30 - International Photographer of the Year
rubrics_metrics.description: Premiere category open to all photographers; work should be of primary interest to a nation or the world and usually intended to be shared nationally/internationally.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Portfolio must include at least two narrative picture stories (5 or more images). To separate stories, create a title slide with white text on a black background and place it at the beginning of each story. Submit a maximum of 50 images, not including title slides. Picture stories are not limited to 10 images. Single images may be included (not required); place single images at the beginning of the portfolio. Photographers may submit only one portfolio into one portfolio category. Copy the title and description into the IPTC title and caption fields.

rubrics_metrics.name: 31 - Photographer of the Year
rubrics_metrics.description: Premiere category open to photographers who work in their own community; honors a photographer who documents their own community.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At least 60% of portfolio must consist of local or regional coverage from photographer's home or organization’s primary geographic market. Only one national or international story is allowed. Portfolio must include at least two narrative picture stories; separate stories with title slides (white text on black) at the beginning of each story. Submit a maximum of 50 images, not including title slides; picture stories not limited to 10 images. Single images may be included and should be placed at the beginning of the portfolio. Fill out IPTC title and caption fields with title and description. If the portfolio consists mostly of national or international stories outside the photographer’s primary market, enter category #30 instead. A portfolio may be submitted once, into either category #30 or #31, but not both.

rubrics_metrics.name: 32 - Sports Photographer of the Year
rubrics_metrics.description: Premiere category open to all photographers; a portfolio should include single pictures and at least one narrative picture story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Picture stories are not limited to 10 images. All single photographs must be taken during 2024. Submit a maximum of 30 photographs. At least three different sports should be represented. Create a title slide with white text on a black background for each story. Fill out IPTC title and caption fields with title and description. Place the slide at the start of each story. Photographers may include sports photographs as part of news portfolios in categories #30 or #31.

rubrics_metrics.name: 33 - Environmental Vision Award
rubrics_metrics.description: Premiere category recognizing a photographer’s long-term story, project, or essay that explores issues related to the environment, natural history, or science.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit a maximum of 40 images. Winning entries from previous years are not allowed. Unpublished stories are allowed; if unpublished, at least 60% of the images should have been created in 2024. Not for coverage of human medical issues or natural disasters unless they are proven results of environmental impact. Project may include a few studio scenes, but they should not make up a majority. Single images and picture stories from this category may be entered in Science & Natural History categories #1 and #2. Images may also be part of a Photographer of the Year portfolio entry if photos were taken or published for the first time in 2024.

rubrics_metrics.name: 34 - Community Awareness Award
rubrics_metrics.description: Premiere category recognizing a photographer’s extended story about the everyday life of people who make up a community, encouraging attention to small events and stories reflecting experiences and dreams of humankind.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A “community” may be a neighborhood, town, commune, rural agricultural area, city subdivision, or socioeconomic region. Submit a maximum of 40 images. Winning entries from previous years are not allowed. If the story has not been published, at least 60% of images must have been created in 2024. Unpublished stories are allowed. Portions of the essay may be entered as a picture story and as part of a Photographer of the Year portfolio entry if photos were taken or first published in 2024.

rubrics_metrics.name: 35 - World Understanding Award
rubrics_metrics.description: Premiere category recognizing a photographer’s long-term project focusing on the human condition, portraying a sense of justice or insight into difficult problems (human relations, world conflict, social injustice, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit a maximum of 40 images. Unpublished stories are allowed. There are no time restrictions; photos need not have been created or first published during 2024. Winning entries from previous years are not allowed; previous entries may not be resubmitted for 5 years. Images from this category may be entered in single or picture story categories only if those images were created in 2024.

rubrics_metrics.name: 36 - Angus McDougall Excellence in Editing Award
rubrics_metrics.description: Category to recognize the best in visual editing by a media organization across all platforms; judges recognize excellence in visual storytelling through photojournalism, video, design and immersive experiences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Open to news organizations, media groups, newspapers, magazines, or specialty advocacy organizations. One portfolio per organization. Include up to 10 stories (print or online); a converged print-and-online version counts as one story. All stories must have been published in 2024. Print story may consist of one or more pages from up to five issues covering a single topic. Online story may include web pages, apps, or other platforms; submit a single active URL link for each story and include required usernames and passwords. Personal portfolios, publications, or websites are not allowed. Business promotions, catalogs, branded content or stories where the funding organization is also the primary subject are not allowed.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 - Photography Book of the Year
rubrics_metrics.description: Category recognizing the best documentary visual storytelling in a book.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Book entries must rely on documentary photography and have been published within the last three years (2022, 2023, or 2024). Previous entries are not eligible. Photographs may be the work of one or more photographers; the photographer and publishing house should coordinate to avoid duplicate entries. Submit 1-10 .jpg thumbnails of the book cover and select pages via Picter. Mail a physical copy (FedEx, DSL, UPS, or postal mail) and include a note with your name and the publisher. Ship the book to the provided POYI/University of Missouri address. NOTE: The book entry does not need to arrive by the contest deadline (Jan. 14, 2024); shipment should be postmarked on or before Jan. 14. Standard courier/postal shipping is sufficient.
